hook: Say you needed {principal, rupees} for three months: a fee, a repair, a deposit on something you want. Here is what each lender in Paisapur would charge you.
prompt: Five ways to get {principal, rupees}. Put them in order, cheapest to pay back first.
choose: Now pick the one you would actually use, or decide not to borrow at all.
summary: You compared what each one really costs to pay back.

family.reveal: {total, rupees} back. No interest, but you owe something that is not money.
family.missed: Nobody would charge you anything. But your uncle would ask about it in front of everyone at dinner, and that costs something too.

bnpl.reveal: {total, rupees} back. Only {monthly, rupees} a month, the smallest of all, which is exactly why it feels cheapest. But it runs for {months} months, not three.
bnpl.missed: A late fee would be added, and it would go on your repayment record.

moneylender.reveal: {total, rupees} back. {rate}% a month, every month: about {yearly}% a year.
moneylender.missed: The interest keeps running, so you would owe more than when you started, and the collector would visit.

loan_app.reveal: {total, rupees} back. The app keeps a {fee}% fee upfront, so you must borrow {borrowed, rupees} to get {principal, rupees}, then pay {rate}% a month on all of it.
loan_app.missed: The app would start calling the contacts in your phone, people who had nothing to do with the loan. That is what it wanted your contact list for.

concept.total_cost: Compare what you pay back in total, not what you pay each month. A small instalment can hide a large total.

monthly_vs_total: {monthly, rupees} a month for {months} months · {total, rupees} paid back in total

result.cheapest_first: Family was cheapest at {family, rupees}. The loan app costs {diff, rupees} more for the same {principal, rupees}.
result.emi_trap: Look at the monthly amounts again. Pay later had the smallest instalment of all, but not the smallest total. A small monthly payment stretched over more months is not a cheaper loan.

missed_title: What if you missed a payment?
missed_intro: Say money got tight one month and you missed a payment:

bank.reveal: {total, rupees} back. {rate}% a month plus a {fee}% fee: slow paperwork, but cheap, and paying on time builds your credit score.
bank.missed: If you missed an EMI: a late fee is added, and a missed payment drops your credit score, which makes the next loan dearer.

none.detail: Wait, save, or find a cheaper way. Not borrowing is always an option.

no_borrow: You chose not to borrow. Often the cheapest loan is the one you never take.
